messages:
Arjun: quick sync  we need to decide how residency rules map to per-API-route policies. Example: account wants EU-only for PII endpoints but allows global for embeddings. How do we express that without exploding config complexity?

Marta: propose per-route residency override. Top-level account.policy.residency applies by default, but each API route can set residency_mode: inherit | strict | prefer | none. Keeps things composable.

Priyanka: +1. We should also support route-scoped allowlists: e.g., routes['/v1/complete-pii'].residency.allowed_regions = [eu-west-1, eu-central-1].

Jon: runtime implications: scorer should evaluate route-level policy first, then account-level fallback. That way teams can lock down sensitive endpoints without touching other traffic.

Arjun: good. Edge-case: difference between "embed-only" vs "generate" endpoints. We should allow policy predicates based on content-class or tag. e.g., account.policy.dynamic_rules = [{predicate: "has_pii:true", residency: "strict"}]

Marta: predicates are powerful but risky. Keep initial v1 simple: route-level config + account default. Delay dynamic content detection to v2 with explicit API flags from SDKs.

Priyanka: UX note: on the account page, show a compact matrix: default residency + per-route overrides. Use icons and short tooltips, not a huge JSON blob.

Jon: security/ops: admin-only emergency bypass header needed for on-call: X-RW-EMERGENCY-REGION: us-east-1. RBAC enforced and requires one-line justification header X-RW-EMERGENCY-REASON. Both are audited.

Arjun: also require a TTL for emergency bypass. Default 10m and auto-expire. Ops must toggle extension.

Marta: pseudocode for routing decision (to include in RFC appendix):
```
policy = route.policy or account.policy
if policy.mode == 'strict': candidates = filter(regions, in(policy.allowed))
else if policy.mode == 'prefer': score = latency + penalty_for_nonpreferred
else: score = latency + capacity_penalty
apply capacity checks
if candidates.empty(): if policy.allow_global_fallback: choose best global and emit audit else return 451
```

Priyanka: add header contract for observability: X-RW-Route-Decisions: route=/v1/complete-pii;region=eu-west-1;reason=policy_strict;fallback=false;ttl=0

Jon: telemetry plan: routing.lookup.latency, routing.policy.violations, routing.fallback.count by route+account. Also expose a per-account summary in Console.

Marta: rollout: canary with synthetic routes. Test matrix: default no-residency, account-level strict, route-level strict, emergency bypass.

ops-bot: Canary flag "per-route-residency" enabled in staging. Telemetry pipelines warming up.

Arjun: testing checklist: 1) preserve KV affinity tags across fallback; 2) ensure cookies/session hints not lost when routing to alternate region; 3) verify audit log entries for each override/bypass.

Priyanka: one more: for Dedicated customers map residency to physical pools: route.policy.allowed_pools = [pool-42, pool-99] and runtime uses pool-level routing rather than region labels. Add to appendix.

Jon: corner case: when a route is strict and only allowed region becomes degraded, prefer returning 451 instead of auto-fallback unless account has allow_global_fallback=true. That reduces regulatory risk.

Marta: okay action items: Arjun + Jon draft RFC appendix (config shape, header contract, telemetry). Priyanka draft Console UX. We'll review tomorrow 30m.

ops-bot: RFC draft branch created: rfc/per-route-residency. Please push appendix PR and mark canary when ready.
